title: Roberto Mancini vows to turn around fortunes of Italian national team
description: Roberto Mancini has vowed to restore the fortunes of the Italian national team and make them “dangerous” again. Former Azzurri striker Mancini began his second spell in charge on Wednesday alongside new technical director Claudio Ranieri.
fullText:
Roberto Mancini has vowed to restore the fortunes of the Italian national team and make them “dangerous” again.

Former Azzurri striker Mancini began his second spell in charge on Wednesday alongside new technical director Claudio Ranieri.

The reappointment of the 61-year-old, who led Italy to the European Championship five years ago, came after a turbulent 24 hours for the country’s football federation.

Italy were seeking a replacement for Gennaro Gattuso, who left the role in April following the nation’s latest failure to qualify for the World Cup.

Andrea Pirlo had been favourite for the job after Pep Guardiola dropped out of the running, but the former midfielder announced on Monday he was no longer in contention amid controversy over his links to a Russian betting firm.

That led newly appointed technical director Paolo Maldini and his adviser Leonardo to leave only days into their roles, with FIGC president Giovanni Malago announcing on Tuesday that Ranieri would succeed Maldini.

Former Manchester City boss Mancini, whose first matches in charge will be against Belgium and Turkey in the Nations League in September, told a press conference: “If Italy go to the World Cup, we become one of the teams to beat.

“Even if we are not favourites, we become dangerous in those tournaments.

“We will try to put together a squad that can qualify for the Euros, after the Nations League, and then think about the World Cup.

“I was here for five years the first time and I was very happy, in my preferred role. We signed a four-year contract now and I hope to win one or two trophies and to hopefully stay even after that, if possible.”

Former Leicester and Chelsea boss Ranieri, who turned down the head coach’s job last year, admitted he was not expecting the call.

“I was at the beach, as you can see from my tan,” he said. “I know it will be a difficult situation, but my career as a coach speaks volumes about dealing with difficulties. I never held back.”

title: Real Madrid youth sensation participating in pre-season under Mourinho wanted by French club
description: Jacobo Ortega is one of many young academy stars participating in the Real Madrid pre-season under new coach Jose Mourinho.With most of the first-team stars currently on an extended break in light of ...
fullText:
Jacobo Ortega is one of many young academy stars participating in the Real Madrid pre-season under new coach Jose Mourinho.

With most of the first-team stars currently on an extended break in light of the FIFA World Cup 2026, Mourinho has taken the opportunity to take a closer look at these academy stars.

Ortega, in particular, is in focus after starring for Castilla last season, impressing onlookers with his goalscoring abilities. But Real Madrid are not the only club observing Ortega.

Ortega enjoyed a fine season with Castilla. (Photo courtesy: Instagram/jacobo.ortegaa)

According to Rodra of ESPN, Strasbourg have set their sights on the young forward, with the French club keen on bringing him to Ligue 1.

Ortega has emerged as one of the biggest sensations to come out of Real Madrid’s academy this season.

A complete forward with a well-rounded skill set, he established himself as a regular starter for Castilla at just 20 years old, catching the eye with his end product in front of goal.

That form has now earned him a place in Mourinho’s plans for pre-season, with the youngster training alongside the first team as the Portuguese coach runs the rule over several academy graduates.

The road to first-team looks tough for Ortega. (Photo by Buda Mendes/Getty Images)

Realistically, though, a path into the Real Madrid first team looks extremely difficult for now.

Kylian Mbappe and Vinicius Jr. remain firmly established at the top of the pecking order in attack, with Vinicius, despite ongoing contract complications and interest from Arsenal, still expected to stay at the Bernabeu for now.

Real Madrid have also added further firepower up top, with Yan Diomande reportedly set to join soon in a deal worth well over €100 million.

On top of that, Endrick has returned to the fold following a successful loan spell at Lyon, while Gonzalo Garcia continues to be retained as part of the squad despite persistent exit links, largely due to his value as a homegrown player under UEFA’s registration rules.

With that level of competition ahead of him, a temporary move away, whether to Strasbourg or elsewhere, could actually represent the smarter path for Ortega to continue his development.

title: Dodgers Not Ruling Out Shohei Ohtani Pitching In Postseason Despite Multiple Injuries
description: Shohei Ohtani is dealing with a knee injury and a biceps injury
fullText:
Los Angeles Dodgers star Shohei Ohtani received an Orthovisc shot in his left knee during the All-Star break and has not been in the rotation since.

Ohtani has been hitting, and he is continuing to show why he is one of the best hitters in baseball. However, he is having a great year on the mound, and the Dodgers will want him healthy for October. He threw a 30-pitch bullpen last week, but has been shut down again after some more knee soreness. Dave Roberts also revealed that he is dealing with an issue in his right biceps, according to MLB.com's Max Ralph.

Roberts noted that the biceps issue popped up in his last start on July 3, and that it is a result of overcompensation for the knee.

"Trying to mitigate that, we stopped the throwing, stopped the bullpens -- hopefully, No. 1, take care of the knee and then not have him try to create velocity with the arm that's not 100%," Roberts said.

Looking for the perfect gift for a baseball player in your life? Check out our brand new baseball lifestyle brand!

As much as the Dodgers want to win now and complete a three-peat, they know that Ohtani is under contract for years to come, and they are interested in building a dynasty that extends beyond just three seasons. They are not going to make any hasty decisions or be impatient with their superstar player. However, Roberts did not rule out a return to the mound.

"Everything that I've heard, that's not the option," Roberts said Tuesday when asked if the team would rule Ohtani out from pitching in October. "I guess anything's possible, but for me, it's highly unlikely. ... If the knee continues to get better and the arm continues to feel better, I would expect him to pitch. I'm trying to give him the best opportunity to be as healthy as possible so he can help us on both ends of the baseball."

Ohtani will continue to hit, and Roberts noted that he is very valuable to the team even as a one-way player.

"If we look at him and his value for our ballclub, we need him in the lineup," Roberts said. "The swing, the running of the bases, the knee, the arm -- it doesn't compromise that. In talking to Shohei and the training staff, that's where we're at."

title: 😱 Peruvian fourth-tier club unveils shirt with a THOUSAND sponsors
description: Have you ever imagined your team having a jersey with a THOUSAND sponsors?That was the solution found by Club Deportivo Municipal to fund the season after being relegated to the Copa Peru, a tournamen...
fullText:
Have you ever imagined your team having a shirt with ONE THOUSAND sponsors?

That was the solution found by Peru’s Club Deportivo Municipal to fund the season after being relegated to the Copa Peru, a tournament equivalent to the Fourth Division.

The campaign “Los Mil Sponsors del Muni” (“The Thousand Sponsors of Muni,” in Portuguese) was launched in January. And it was a huge success.

It took just three months for a large part of the one thousand small spaces to be sold for 200 Peruvian soles each (around R$ 300).

"An initiative that challenges conventional sports marketing, with a new sponsorship program. One thousand spaces available for businesses and ventures at affordable prices, an innovation through which, together, we add up the amount needed to take the club back to the place it deserves," the club said at the time of the initiative’s launch.

About R$ 302,600 was raised, which made all the difference in keeping the club active.

The shirt came to feature hundreds of black-and-white squares with space for interested sponsors, while keeping the crest on the traditional red diagonal sash.

Which created a "pixelated" effect.

Pre-sales of the shirts began last Saturday (25). With a discount for those who became sponsors.

Despite all the effort and innovation, Muni was unsuccessful in staying alive in the Copa Perú.

They qualified for the second phase of the Liga Departamental de Lima after eliminating Defensor Santa Tereza, but were knocked out by Sport Humaya last Sunday (26).

The champion will secure direct promotion to Liga 2, the second division, in 2027. The runner-up, meanwhile, will play in the Third Division next season.

Deportivo Municipal are the fifth most successful club in the top tier of Peruvian football, with four titles (1938, 1940, 1943 and 1950).

They have played in one edition of the Copa Libertadores (going out in the very first preliminary round in 2017) and four editions of the Copa Sudamericana (2015, 16, 18 and 19).

title: Steven Wright: Interest growing in girls flag football, yet few area schools ready to make the leap
description: * Save Multiple schools in the Miami Valley have indicated they do not plan to add girls flag football to their list of athletic programs. Cox First Media surveyed area high schools about their interest in offering girls flag football as a varsity activity following its approval by the OHSAA as its 29th sport. No area school that responded to the survey provided a “yes”-type response outside ...
fullText:
Multiple schools in the Miami Valley have indicated they do not plan to add girls flag football to their list of athletic programs.

Cox First Media surveyed area high schools about their interest in offering girls flag football as a varsity activity following its approval by the OHSAA as its 29th sport. No area school that responded to the survey provided a “yes”-type response outside of the schools that already offer the sport.

School administrators did provide positive feedback on the sport’s growth and acceptance by the OHSAA.

Northmont athletic director Micah Harding indicated the school is not in a position to add any new programs as it attempts to avoid further expenses, but believes it could be something that is explored in a better financial situation.

Sustainability is also on the mind when it comes to growth. Miamisburg AD Jason Shade believes it would be difficult to ensure a program could make it through its infancy due to declining enrollment and a low percentage of upperclassmen females.

The established spring sports in place at many schools already have the attention of many student-athletes, according to several responses.

“That said, we will continue to have conversations internally and gather feedback from our student-athletes and families regarding future interest,” Shade said.

Bellbrook AD Charlie O’Dell said he is happy to have added several girls sports in recent years, including wrestling, bowling and golf, but the total number of sports offered when compared to the district’s steady enrollment numbers does not create the opportunity to add anything more.

Those that already have the sport are proud to be at the forefront.

The 2027 season will be the third year Trotwood has offered the sport. AD Jonas Smith said he is excited about its potential future. The school has also added flag football as a middle school sport.

“Flag football has generated tremendous enthusiasm among our student-athletes, and our young ladies have thoroughly enjoyed the opportunity to participate and compete,” Smith said.

The sport will continue to have a place in the area as it enters its first full season as part of the OHSAA. Trotwood, Badin, and all six Dayton City League members fielded teams in the 2026 Spring season.

Badin were the inaugural state champions in 2025 as part of the Ohio High School Football Coaches Association tournament and reached the first sponsored OHSAA state tournament in 2026.

Ponitz CTC has won three consecutive city league titles.

Girls flag football became the 29th sport recognized by the OHSAA in June and made Ohio the 40th state in the country to offer it. The OHSAA now sponsors more girls sports (15) than boys (14) and says 162 schools — the majority being in the greater-Cincinnati and Cleveland area — participated during the 2026 Spring season.

Dates and sites for the 2027 state championships are to be determined. The finals were held at Massillon’s Paul Brown Tiger Stadium and Tom Benson Hall of Fame Stadium in Canton the past two seasons.

title: MLB insider would be 'shocked' if Giants traded their $313.5 million slugger
description: This expensive Giants slugger getting traded would be a shocker.
fullText:
MLB insider would be 'shocked' if Giants traded their $313.5 million slugger originally appeared on The Sporting News. Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here.

The San Francisco Giants are going to be trade deadline sellers this season, and there are plenty of interesting names worth considering at this year's deadline from the Giants' roster.

Luis Arraez and Robbie Ray are the two headliners as rental options, but Heliot Ramos is another player who could fetch some legitimate trade interest. However, the Giants might also entertain trade offers on some expensive veterans this summer.

For MLB insider Andy McCullough of The Athletic, he would be "shocked" if the Giants traded $313.5 million slugger Rafael Devers at the trade deadline for a simple reason: his contract.

"I would be absolutely shocked - shocked! - if the Giants could move Devers' contract," McCullough writes.

For as good a hitter as Devers is, posting a solid .796 OPS this season after a very slow start to the year, the Giants would be hard-pressed to find a team willing to take on his contract.

Devers is in the middle of a massive 10-year, $313.5 million contract that runs through the 2033 season. Such a large and lengthy contract is a real problem for the Giants in potential trade conversations.

MORE: Giants willing to trade Heliot Ramos in big news for many MLB clubs

Teams would likely ask the Giants to take on some of that contract to consider a trade, and if the Giants did somehow find a team willing to take on his deal, the other team probably wouldn't want to give up much in return.

The Giants are, effectively, stuck with Devers, barring some unforeseen interest from a desperate MLB team. For now, Devers is a Giant and doesn't look likely to be leaving anytime soon.

Devers would be a good trade target if he weren't so expensive, especially for someone who's a DH-only or a questionable defensive first baseman.

There is almost no chance Devers is traded now, or in the future. His $313.5 million contract is a massive hurdle to a deal, and McCullough, like the rest of the baseball world, would be "shocked" if the Giants somehow found a trade partner for Devers.

title: Former Detroit Lions S Ifeatu Melifonwu Finds New Home
description: Former Detroit Lions safety Ifeatu Melifonwu has agreed to a one-year contract with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.
fullText:
Former Detroit Lions safety Ifeatu Melifonwu has landed another NFL opportunity.

The Tampa Bay Buccaneers have agreed to a one-year contract with Melifonwu, according to ESPN’s Adam Schefter. The move gives Tampa Bay an experienced and versatile defensive back shortly after training camp opened.

Melifonwu spent the 2025 season with the Miami Dolphins after leaving Detroit in free agency.

The 27-year-old appeared in 16 games and made eight starts for Miami, producing a career-high 53 tackles, one interception and one sack. He also defended one pass during his lone season with the Dolphins.

Tampa Bay will now get a defender capable of lining up at safety, cornerback or closer to the line of scrimmage. Melifonwu’s combination of size and athleticism has always made him intriguing, though injuries prevented him from consistently establishing himself during his first four NFL seasons.

Detroit selected Melifonwu in the third round of the 2021 NFL Draft.

His best season with the Lions came in 2023, when he recorded 33 tackles, three sacks, eight passes defended and two interceptions. His late-season surge included several impact plays during Detroit’s run to the NFC Championship Game.

Injuries limited Melifonwu to only three games in 2024, and the Lions allowed him to leave the following offseason. He signed a one-year deal with Miami and responded by playing the most defensive snaps of his career.

Across five NFL seasons, Melifonwu has appeared in 53 games with 22 starts, collecting 125 tackles, 5.5 sacks and three interceptions.

Ifeatu Melifonwu’s Lions career never developed as consistently as Detroit hoped, but his talent has never been difficult to see.

After putting together a productive season in Miami, the former Lions safety has earned another opportunity with Tampa Bay. His versatility and starting experience should give him a legitimate chance to carve out a role in the Buccaneers’ secondary.

title: What to expect from the Audi Summer Tour 2026
description: FC Bayern head off on the Audi Summer Tour for the tenth time – and this time the German champions are going back to Asia from 1 to 8 August! The trip will initially take them to the island of J...
fullText:
FC Bayern head off on the Audi Summer Tour for the tenth time – and this time the German champions are going back to Asia from 1 to 8 August! The trip will initially take them to the island of Jeju in South Korea, and then onto the bustling metropolis of Hong Kong. As sporting highlights, there are two friendlies lined up, while fans can also look forward to attractive events and open training sessions. We’ll be keeping you up to date on the tour with daily coverage on our website fcbayern.com, in the official FC Bayern app and on our social media channels.

Here’s what you can look forward to in South Korea and Hong Kong as well as on our platforms:

On Tuesday 4 August, FC Bayern will play Korean Red&Gold partner club Jeju SK FC. Then on Friday 7 August, Vincent Kompany’s side go up against Europa League winners Aston Villa in the Audi Football Summit at the Kai Tak Stadium in Hong Kong. You can watch live streams of both matches on FC Bayern TV PLUS. As usual, we’ll report live from the stadium for you. Whether it’s live text commentary, the match report, post-match reaction or press conference, you won’t miss a thing with us!

If you want to be there yourself, tickets can be purchased from this link. Information for fans attending the match on Jeju can be found here, while information for the match against Aston Villa in Hong Kong is available from this link.

As well as the games against Jeju SK FC and Aston Villa, we’re showing other pre-season friendlies on FC Bayern TV PLUS:

Live streams of FC Bayern's friendlies

FC Bayern boss Kompany will continue to work on getting his players into top form in South Korea and Hong Kong. We’ll be there to report on all the proceedings on  fcbayern.com, the FC Bayern app and the social media channels. Two dates in particular should be marked in your calendars: the German champions will hold an open training session at the Jeju World Cup Stadium on Monday 3 August at 18:00 local times (11:00 CEST), and again at the same local time on Thursday 6 August at the Kai Tak Stadium. Note that the open session in Hong Kong starts at 12:00 CEST.

With our free live stream (website, app, YouTube, Facebook and Twitch – except in South Korea), you can also watch our players hard at work virtually on both days.

On the day before each friendly and an hour before the open training sessions, Kompany and one FCB player will answer questions from journalists. We’re streaming the press conferences on 3 and 6 August from 17:00 local time (10:00 CEST Jeju, 11:00 CEST Hong Kong) live and for free on the website, app, YouTube, Facebook and Twitch.

First stage of the trip takes in the 'Audi Summer Tour'

If you happen to be in Jeju at the same time, then come along! Before the open training session and the match the next day, there’ll be a fan zone with Bayern legends and mascot Berni at the World Cup Stadium.

If you'd like to get in the mood for FC Bayern in Hong Kong, you can stop by the Lan Fong Yuen Milk Tea Shop as of now. At this gathering spot for Bayern fans in the city, everyone can stock up on stickers, FC Bayern-themed cups, snacks and drinks.

On 5 August from 20:00, supporters can purchase the latest products from the FC Bayern Pop-Up Store on Nelson Street in Hong Kong and get autographs from Bayern legends. On 6 August from 12:00, fans of the German record champions have the opportunity to meet our former striker Roy Makaay at the Pop-Up Store in the Kai Tak Mall.

This store in Jeju is open from 1 to 4 August: World Cup Stadium.

These stores in Hong Kong are open until the end of the Tour: Kai Tak Sports Park Mall; Sneaker Street, Mongkok, Kowloon (all already open); Hong Kong Airport & The Forest Plaza, Mongkok, Kowloon (both open 31 July).

From challenges with the Bayern stars and behind-the-scenes reports to partner activations and fan events – we can promise you: we’ll keep you up to date on the varied programme and numerous events on the Audi Summer Tour 2026 on our club media channels. Bring it on!

Get tickets for the friendlies on the Audi Summer Tour now:

Tickets for games against Jeju SK and Aston Villa

title: Champions League star hospitalized after being 'yanked out of car by armed gangsters'
description: Union Saint-Gilloise winger Mohammed Fuseini was hospitalized after being pulled from his vehicle by a masked gang during a robbery in the Belgian city of Brussels on Sunday
fullText:
A UEFA Champions League soccer star competing in Belgium's top flight was hospitalized after being targeted by a masked gang during a violent robbery.

Union Saint-Gilloise winger Mohammed Fuseini was dragged from his vehicle in Brussels on Sunday morning (July 26), with disturbing footage of the assault spreading across social media. The 24-year-old Ghanaian international, who missed out on his country's FIFA World Cup roster, is seen being seized by a masked gang, reportedly armed, and placed in a headlock.

Local outlet Het Laatste Nieuws (HLN) reported that Fuseini had a Rolex valued at up to €14,000 (roughly $16,000) stolen. Video footage also captured the group attempting to steal Fuseini's phone as he fought back. However, he was ultimately overpowered by the five-person gang, as per The Mirror US.

Wrexham fans set to gather in New York ahead of landmark Liverpool match at Yankee Stadium

The attackers eventually released him before fleeing the scene. Clips of the assault have since gone viral online, particularly in his home country of Ghana.

The harrowing incident was allegedly recorded by an unidentified teammate of Fuseini, who was subsequently taken to the hospital for medical treatment.

His club, Union SG, released a statement updating supporters on Fuseini's condition following the brazen daylight robbery. They said: "The images from last Sunday are particularly harrowing.

"He subsequently went to the hospital for a check-up and received excellent care there from the Brussels police, whom we sincerely thank for their outstanding work.

To listen to the latest episode of 'All Out Soccer' - CLICK HERE

"The injuries are not serious, and he resumed training yesterday."

The public prosecutor's office has also weighed in on the matter, confirming that three individuals were targeted in a robbery carried out by the group.

In an official statement, authorities revealed that multiple people had allegedly been assaulted, with stolen items including watches, phones, and other personal possessions subsequently recovered.

A suspect, reported to be 23 years old, has since been identified and placed in custody.

title: FIFA's plan to sell World Cup to private investors met with shock and anger by the world of football
description: FIFA president Gianni Infantino has written to all 211 member associations, offering each $40 million (€35 million) if they back his controversial plan to sell stakes in the governing body's major competitions.
fullText:
A proposal that could reshape the commercial future of the World Cup has sparked fierce opposition from football's governing bodies.

FIFA president Gianni Infantino on Tuesday unveiled plans to create a $20 billion (€17.5 billion) company, FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE), to run competitions including the World Cup and Club World Cup with private investors, according to The Times of London.

Former FIFA president Sepp Blatter voiced concern over the close ties between Infantino and US President Donald Trump, as one of the reported potential investors is the family of Trump's son-in-law, Jared Kushner. Meanwhile, EU Commissioner for Sport Glenn Micallef wrote on X: "Hands off our game."

From Europe to Asia and the Americas, football governing bodies have voiced concern over FIFA's proposal. Euronews looks at some of the key reactions.

UEFA was among the first organisations to condemn the proposal. European football's governing body made clear that football is not for sale, warning against turning the sport into a commercial asset.

“This crosses a line that football’s governing institutions should never cross. UEFA takes it extremely seriously. So should every National Football Association,” said UEFA in a fiery statement released shortly after the Times article was released.

“The soul and governance of football are not assets to trade — especially with zero transparency as to who gains financially,” UEFA said Tuesday, responding to the reports of selling stakes in FIFA competitions.

UEFA vice-president Gabriele Gravina has also criticised FIFA's proposal.

"Football cannot be reduced to a private affair," Gravina said.

"We are crossing the line. The balance laboriously constructed over the years between show football and football, a great popular passion - continues the former FIGC No. 1 - risks being swept away by a business vision that is not good for the movement."

UEFA will hold an emergency meeting on Wednesday to discuss its response to FIFA's controversial private investor plans, according to French sports minister Marina Ferrari.

"I acknowledge the emergency meeting to be held Wednesday among European football authorities. Faced with a project that could profoundly transform the balance of our sport, it is essential that European stakeholders speak with a single voice," Ferrari said in a social media post.

La Liga president Javier Tebas lashed out at Infantino, accusing him of mixing "politics, discipline, money and power without transparency."

In his X post, which featured an iceberg, the visible section read "What is already known," while the submerged section read "This is only the tip of the iceberg," suggesting that much more about Infantino's stewardship of FIFA remains to be revealed.

"And now FIFA is promising more than $10 billion and up to an additional $20 million for each member association, while at the same time preparing to bring private investors into its rights and competitions. This does not look like reform. It looks like an election campaign financed at the expense of football's future," he wrote.

"Development cannot be used to buy votes or silence criticism. FIFA's competitions and commercial rights are not Infantino's personal property.

Anyone who mixes politics, discipline, money and power without transparency cannot lead anything. Infantino is not the solution to FIFA's governance. He is the problem. We are only scratching the surface of the iceberg."

England's Football Association (FA) said it had not been informed of FIFA's proposal before it emerged publicly and raised concerns about the way it had been handled.

The governing body said it was "deeply concerned about the lack of process and governance to get to this point, and the apparent substance and principles involved."

"When the proposal is shared in the full and transparent way now promised by FIFA, we will make our views clear, and comment further," a spokesperson said, adding that they were "completely unaware" of the proposal.

The German Football Association (DFB) has joined UEFA in criticising FIFA President Gianni Infantino's reported plan to sell a 20-30% stake in the World Cup to private investors, with DFB Vice-President Hans-Joachim Watzke saying "a line has been crossed."

"Many in European football see FIFA's plans as a direct attack on the sport. I share that view," said Watzke, who also serves as a UEFA Executive Committee vice-president.

"There is broad consensus among the member associations. That has become clear to me in several discussions over the past few days with Aleksander Ceferin and other colleagues," he added. Watzke also stressed Europe's importance to the World Cup.

"At the 2026 World Cup, six European teams reached the quarter-finals and three made the semi-finals. If European football stands united against these plans, that carries significant weight".

Philippe Diallo, president of the French Football Federation, also criticised the complete lack of communication surrounding the proposal.

"We learned about this very significant project through a press release. We have no details, and given its direction – namely bringing investment funds into a commercial company alongside FIFA – it raises many questions," Diallo said.

He added that national football associations had not been consulted and had been given no concrete information that would allow them to take a position on what he described as issues that are fundamental to the future of the sport.

Diallo also said he would immediately begin discussions with the presidents of Europe's leading football associations to determine how to respond to FIFA's plans.

"Starting today, I will be in contact with my counterparts at the major European football associations to determine how we should approach these plans, about which we have received no specific information," he said.

UEFA issues angry response to FIFA boss Infantino's plan to sell World Cup stakes to investors

Concerns have also spread beyond Europe, with football governing bodies in Asia, North and Central America and the Caribbean, and South America all calling for greater transparency and a more inclusive consultation process before taking a position on FIFA's proposal.

"The AFC was not consulted on the proposal and is disappointed that a matter of such significance entered the public domain before the AFC family had been afforded the opportunity to examine and discuss it through the appropriate and established governance channels," Asian Football Confederation said in a statement.

"While the AFC recognises the importance of exploring innovative approaches that can strengthen the future of global football, initiatives of this scale and consequence must be founded upon the principles of good governance, transparency and meaningful consultation."

CONCACAF, the governing body for football in North and Central America and the Caribbean, also voiced concerns over the proposal. Its president, Victor Montagliani, said the confederation had not been consulted before FIFA unveiled its plans.

“Concacaf was only made aware of this matter through media reports and, subsequently, via a media release,” Concacaf said in a statement.

“We are deeply concerned by the lack of due process."

“As leaders within football, we are the custodians of the game. Collectively, FIFA, the confederations and every member association have a responsibility to always act in the best interests of the sport. Every decision we make must be guided by good governance, robust processes and long-term stewardship."

FIFA has given its member associations until 19 September to So far, however, the offer has done little to quell criticism, with many football governing bodies united in calling for greater transparency and consultation.

title: Lloyd pays tribute to 'greatest' Sobers at funeral
description: Sir Garfield Sobers is called the "greatest all-round cricketer the world has ever known" by former team-mate Sir Clive Lloyd at the legendary West Indies player's state funeral in Barbados.
fullText:
Sir Garfield Sobers was called the "greatest all-round cricketer the world has ever known" by former team-mate Sir Clive Lloyd at the legendary West Indies player's state funeral in Barbados.

Lloyd described all-rounder Sobers, who died aged 89 on 17 July, as "a man who lived in the hearts and minds of Caribbean people and who became a source of inspiration to millions throughout the world".

An entertaining left-handed batter and bowler of seam and spin, Sobers played 93 Tests between 1954 and 1974, scoring 8,032 runs and taking 235 wickets.

The funeral was staged at the Kensington Oval in Bridgetown, the principle ground in Barbados and home to a pavilion named after Sobers.

Lloyd and fellow West Indies legends Brian Lara and Desmond Haynes were among those who spoke at the state service of thanksgiving, which was also attended by Barbados president Jeffrey Bostic, prime minister Mia Mottley and Barbadian music superstar Rihanna.

West Indies Test captain Roston Chase, who comes from Barbados, vice-captain Jomel Warrican and the current side's Barbadian players were also in attendance, having completed a Test victory over Pakistan on Monday, winning by 90 runs inside four days in Trinidad.

"Sir Garfield Sobers was not merely the outstanding cricketer of his generation," Lloyd added. "He brought to the beautiful game a rare combination of brilliance, imagination, courage and joy."

Sobers' coffin was draped in the flag of Barbados and set off from the Parliament Buildings in Bridgetown on a gun carriage for a formal procession through the nation's capital.

On arrival at the stadium, the carriage passed through a guard of honour of raised cricket bats.

"This is not a sad moment," Lara said of his mentor. "This is a moment for us to celebrate and I hope you feel the same. Today we celebrate the remarkable life of the greatest all-round cricketer.

"We celebrate a man who gave so much to his family, to Barbados, to the West Indies and all of us who had the privilege of knowing him."

Sobers scored 365 not out against Pakistan in 1958 - an effort which stood as the record Test score for 36 years.

He was also named one of Wisden's five cricketers of the 20th century.

During his stint at Nottinghamshire in 1968, Sobers became the first player to hit a six off all six balls in an over in a first-class match.

Mottley described Sobers as "a man who if he had not achieved any of those great feats on the cricket field would have been immortalised by his community as a good man and a great man".

Reverend Canon Guy Hewitt read out a message from King Charles during the service.

"History is distinguished with sporting champions whose records have rightly commanded respect across generations," the message read. "There have been far fewer however whose name along brings a smile to people's faces across Barbados, the Caribbean and the Commonwealth.

"Sir Garfield Sobers belongs very firmly in the latter category. I send my deepest sympathies to Sir Garry's family as they come to terms with this great loss."

Sobers' body lay in state at the Barbados parliament on Monday and at the Kensington Oval on Tuesday, with national dignitaries and members of the public able to pay their respects.

He will be laid to rest at Coral Ridge Memorial Gardens in the south of Barbados.

title: Silver for record-breaking swimmer Richards
description: Matt Richards creates Wales swimming history by winning a fourth Commonwealth medal at one Games.
fullText:
Matt Richards has created Wales swimming history by winning a fourth Commonwealth medal at one Games.

Richards, 23, claimed silver in the 200m freestyle alongside James Guy after the Englishman recorded the same time with Australian Kai Taylor taking the gold.

Only Valerie Davies in the first Games in 1930 and Michael Richards and Martyn Woodroffe 40 years later had previously managed three medals in one Games.

Matthew Richards has now surpassed them with his tally of two silver and two bronze with the swimmer having not won a Commonwealth Games medal before Glasgow.

He was part of two bronze relay squads before claiming his first individual podium position with silver in the 100m freestyle on Tuesday night.

Wales have won six medals in the pool with three silver and three bronze, which is an improvement on the two third place finishes in Birmingham in 2022.

title: Leeds United Willing To Ship Off 26-Year-Old Outcast: Does It Make Sense For The Next Season?
description: The numbers tell one side of the story for Joel Piroe. 19 goals. Four assists. 45 appearances. Top scorer in the Championship in 2024/25 and the main engine behind getting Leeds United back to the big...
fullText:
The numbers tell one side of the story for Joel Piroe. 19 goals. Four assists. 45 appearances. Top scorer in the Championship in 2024/25 and the main engine behind getting Leeds United back to the big time. Yet, stroll around West Yorkshire right now, and you quickly realise statistics mean precious little when a manager’s mind is made up that he is a low-priority man. Daniel Farke wants a new leading man. Simple as that.

Farke wants a traditional centre-forward to hold up the ball, bully centre-backs, and trigger the team’s pressing system off the ball. They have Dominic Calvert-Lewin for that. That leaves Joel Piroe in a tough spot.

Despite doing everything asked of him last season, the 26-year-old Dutchman finds himself pushed right to the edge of the first-team picture. Farke clearly harbours doubts about whether Piroe has the raw pace, athletic engine, and mobility required to lead the line in the top flight.

With just 12 months remaining on his contract at Elland Road, the hierarchy seems open to business. A cut-price departure before deadline day is now a genuine possibility, with Birmingham City already keeping close tabs on the situation.

LEEDS, ENGLAND – MARCH 03: Joel Piroe of Leeds United reacts during the Premier League match between Leeds United and Sunderland at Elland Road on March 03, 2026 in Leeds, England. (Photo by George Wood/Getty Images)

Let’s be realistic about what lies ahead. Top-tier survival is a bloody business. Turning your back on a player who delivered 19 league goals for promotion is a massive risk, no matter how limited his defensive work might look on a tactical board. Critics constantly point out his flaws. He doesn’t sprint 50 yards to close down defenders. He isn’t going to out-muscle massive international centre-halves in physical battles.

None of that changes the basic truth: the man knows where the back of the net is. Finding players with that natural instinct inside the penalty box costs serious money in today’s market. Whatever small fee Leeds United collect by shipping Piroe off to the Midlands won’t even cover half the cost of replacing those nineteen goals.

Cashing in on a proven goalscorer for a small fee during a summer of massive transition is short-sighted. Farke can bring in his physical focal point without throwing Piroe out the door for cheap.

Think about the grind of a top-flight campaign. Late in matches, when defenders are gassed and tired, bringing on an instinctive finisher off the bench changes everything. You don’t need him to press for 90 minutes; you need him to sniff out one chance in the six-yard box. Keep the player, adjust his role, and hold onto that finishing instinct. Selling him now for next to nothing is a mistake Leeds will regret the second results turn sour.

title: Trump’s ‘embarrassing’ comment about LeBron has ESPN host speaking up: ‘Beyond the pale"
description: The president cited his friendship with Michael Jordan when asked to weigh in on the greatest of all time debate.
fullText:
It’s no secret that ESPN host Stephen A. Smith and NBA star LeBron James don’t get along.

On Monday, Smith defended James after President Donald Trump called James “racist” last week when taking questions from reporters.

This, even for a hot take machine like Smith, was “beyond the pale.”

“It’s embarrassing,” Smith said in a video posted on YouTube. “You’re the commander-in-chief, you’re the president of the United States, and you’re going to come out and you’re going to call this black man, who’s universally recognized one of the greatest athletes who have ever lived, who has been an upstanding citizen, somebody I don’t get along with, and I’m still willing to concede he’s great.”

Smith argued that Trump is resorting to calling James racist simply because James has never supported Trump politically.

James endorsed Hillary Clinton in 2016, Joe Biden in 2020, and Kamala Harris in 2024.

“The only Democratic candidate LeBron James ever really stood up for was Barack Obama,” Smith said. “Everything since then has basically been anti-Trump over the last three elections.”

Last week, Trump claimed new Philadelphia 76ers superstar might be “a racist” after weighing in on the debate over who is the greatest basketball player of all time.

When Trump responded to the question from Fox News’ Peter Doocy on Friday, the president pointed to his personal relationship and not statistics to settle the debate between James and Chicago Bulls legend Michael Jordan.

“Well, Michael Jordan’s a guy that’s a friend of mine — play golf with him. He’s a really good guy. And I think LeBron is — maybe he’s a racist. But maybe he doesn’t like Trump, I don’t know. But I only like people that like me. So I would say Michael Jordan all the way,” Trump said.

title: The motion-sickness cure hidden in iPhone settings
description: A buried iPhone setting is turning heads and saving stomachs. But does relief just mean more time staring at your screen?
fullText:
A buried iPhone setting is turning heads and saving stomachs. But does relief just mean more time staring at your screen?

I try not to look at other people's phones, but you get unintentional glances jammed in the crowds on the New York subway, bodies lurching around as the train blasts through tunnels. Lately I've noticed something strange. I keep seeing people with dots dancing across their screens.

The more I saw it, the more I needed to know. It turns out all these people have something in common: they get motion sickness.

This choreographed dot ballet is a lesser-known iPhone setting called "Vehicle Motion Cues" that's supposed to help. It puts animated dots on the edges of your screen, which move in sync with the motion of the vehicle you're in, thanks to the phone's accelerometer.

Reviews are mixed, but over the past few months, some people have gone wild for it. One man I met on the subway told me he loves the feature so much he keeps it on 24 hours a day, even when he's not moving – though he declined to share his name with the strange journalist asking questions on his commute.

The dots could be an antidote if you're cursed with a history of queasy car rides. I was born with an iron stomach, so I'm afraid I can't relate. But I think there's something more interesting happening. Bit by bit, our devices are adapting to infiltrate more of our lives.

Here's some trivia I learned talking to doctors for this story: it seems like most of the people who study motion sickness get motion sickness.

"When I go on a cruise, I'm in my bunk for like 72 to 96 hours. I can't eat, I can't get up," says Tom Stoffregen, professor emeritus at the University of Minnesota, US, who's been studying motion sickness since the 1980s.

Experts disagree about what causes motion sickness. The classic explanation is "sensory conflict theory": your inner ear detects movement, but other senses (like your sight) see a bunch of fixed objects that seem like they aren't going anywhere.

Stoffregen doesn't buy it. Instead, he says the issue is your muscles and other bodily systems are constantly guessing where you're about to move to control your posture, and you get discombobulated when the prediction fails. That might explain why passengers get sick but drivers usually don't, because they're controlling the car.

Either way, the confusion makes some of us nauseous, says Kristen Steenerson, a clinical associate professor at Stanford University, US, who studies the vestibular system, which controls balance.

"That deviation is what makes people feel dizzy, or disoriented," says Steenerson. "And probably due to some interesting evolutionary coincidences, that elicits a lot of nausea." We may have evolved to assume we've eaten something toxic when we feel disoriented, she says, so your body thinks it a good time to vomit.

If you can give your body signals that demonstrate how you're moving through space, it can mitigate motion sickness, Steenerson says. The iPhone's dots seem to follow the same logic. "They give you a sense of how you are moving in space," she says.

"There is some research that has looked into visual feedback and found it can be very helpful," says Steenerson. For example, you can buy phenomenally goofy anti-nausea glasses that are filled with liquid that sloshes around in a similar fashion, and there's evidence they work. If you've never seen them, I am delighted to present you with the photo below.

Steenerson says the dots help a little with her own motion sickness. "Everyone thinks there's something wrong with my screen. These dots are so cool," she says.

To turn it on, open your iPhone Settings > Accessibility > Motion > Vehicle Motion Cues. You can leave the dots on perpetually or have them turn on automatically when your phone detects motion. Android apps can replicate the setting, and there are rumours a similar feature is coming to Pixel phones.

You can also change the size and colour. I've been walking around with big purple dots on my screen that make for great conversation starters.

Some motion sickness victims told me vehicle motion cues didn't help, but some people call them a miracle.

Zandie Brockett, a curator from New York City, swears by them. "It's been a game changer," she says, enough to turn her into an iPhone-dots evangelist. "I'm not screaming about them from the rooftops. But I recommend them anytime someone tells me they get car sick," she says.

I heard the same from my old boss, Rory Carroll. His car sickness is particularly ironic, as he spends a lot of time in the passenger's seat for work: he's editor-in-chief of Alloy, a car enthusiast news publication. "It's a bit of an occupational hazard," Caroll says. "It's solving a very specific problem that I've had my whole life. The dots really work."

Fans of the iPhone dots kept telling me the same observation. They are only useful when you get motion sick because you're looking at your phone.

In other words, your reward is yet another opportunity to look at your screen. Which isn't a reward at all, perhaps, when so many people worry about screen time. "It is a bit of a bummer to have one less reason not to look at Instagram," says Carroll.

• Is your tech giving you phone body?

• Your phone's blue light isn't ruining your sleep

• The saddest question on the internet: Is that cat real?

Phones consume modern life, and new developments are letting them creep into the few remaining times we can't use them. Ever-growing battery life means screens stay on for longer. Elon Musk and his competitors have blanketed the sky with satellites that beam Wi-Fi and phone service to once disconnected areas.

There's even a rumour that Apple is working AirPods with cameras in them, not for taking photos, but to serve as eyes for new AI voice tools you can use screen-free. It may allow for new computing opportunities in those rare phoneless moments, like when you're walking down the street.

If looking at screens makes you car sick, you might want to try the iPhone dots. Or – stop me if this sounds crazy – you could just put your phone down and enjoy the ride.

title: A Dark-Money Campaign Is Paying Influencers to Frame Chinese AI as a Threat
description: Build American AI, a nonprofit linked to a super PAC bankrolled by executives at OpenAI and Andreessen Horowitz, is funding a campaign to spread pro-AI messaging and stoke fears about China.
fullText:
video posted on April 1, lifestyle influencer Melissa Strahle poses outdoors before an American flag as soft instrumental music plays. “AI lets me focus on what matters most,” she tells her 1.4 million followers. “We need to invest in American-made AI to ensure America leads the way in innovation and job creation.”

Strahle labeled the post an advertisement, but she didn’t disclose what organization had paid for it. It turns out the funding came from Build American AI, a dark-money group tied to Leading the Future, a $100 million super PAC supported by, and in some cases directly funded by, tech figures affiliated with companies like OpenAI and Palantir.

The video is part of a coordinated influence campaign that Build American AI is funding, which is being rolled out on social media in two phases. The first focused on working with lifestyle influencers like Strahle, who did not respond to a request for comment, to promote the US artificial intelligence industry and American innovation. But the second and current phase of the campaign is all about China.

Marketing agencies are pitching influencers deals such as $5,000 per TikTok video to amplify Build American AI’s messaging about how China’s technological rise should be seen as a threat. The goal, according to a staffer from SM4, the influencer marketing agency running the campaign on behalf of Build American AI, is to subtly shift public debate by framing China’s AI advancement as a serious risk to the safety and well-being of Americans.

“They want a push to mention China and America and why beating China is so important,” says the staffer.

Sample messaging provided by Build American AI to content creators includes lines like “I just learned that China is trying really hard to beat the US in AI. If they do, it could mean that China gets personal data from me and my kids, and take jobs that should be here in the US In the AI innovation race, I’m Team USA!!!”

WIRED first learned about the campaign after this article’s author was invited by SM4 to participate. The details were later confirmed by several other content creators who received similar outreach.

Josh Murphy, an ecologist with over 130,000 followers on Instagram who says he did not respond to SM4’s offer, explains that while he’s “not necessarily against AI,” combining generic praise for the technology with aggressive anti-China messaging felt off to him. “AI can absolutely be utilized for the betterment of humanity,” Murphy says, “but this unregulated industry that we have right now, where it’s just wacky tech bros that are pursuing greed at the expense of everything else, is just not what it’s supposed to be.”

“The United States has an opportunity to remain the global leader in AI innovation, and we’re taking that message to the broadest possible audience through an all-of-the-above communications strategy,” Jesse Hunt, a spokesperson representing Leading the Future, said of the campaign. “Dark money doomer groups have spent millions spreading misinformation to the American public, and we won’t let it go unchallenged. We’ll continue to highlight AI’s economic benefits, counter false narratives, and build the coalition needed to advance a national regulatory framework using every tool at our disposal.”

Supporters of Leading the Future include OpenAI president and cofounder Greg Brockman, venture capitalist and Palantir cofounder Joe Lonsdale, venture capital firm Andreessen Horowitz, and AI company Perplexity, according to the PAC. Leading the Future says it has received $140 million in total contributions and commitments, with $51 million available to spend to push its pro-AI agenda as of April. The news site NOTUS called the group a “massive political war chest for the AI industry.”

title: What We Think the 2026 Gartner Hype Cycle Gets Right About GraphQL
description: American Airlines built its API orchestration layer before AI agents existed, then used it as the agent layer. See why using GraphQL is the real head start.
fullText:
What We Think the 2026 Gartner Hype Cycle Gets Right About GraphQL

GraphQL is in Gartner’s Trough of Disillusionment in the 2026 Gartner® Hype Cycle™ for APIs. Good.

The trough is what happens when expectations set during the hype phase meet the reality of actual production requirements. People stop hyping and start asking the key questions: Does this thing work? Does it solve a problem we actually have? Can we operate it in production without making everyone miserable?

Those are the right questions, and any proposed platform tech has to answer them.

With GraphQL in the trough, Gartner notes this observation:

“Despite the potential, GraphQL adoption for AI and agentic workflows have not translated to increased adoption due to its limited penetration in key agentic use cases.”

That strikes us as basically right. MCP and other agent-oriented protocols arrived with an obvious, legible connection to AI. GraphQL, like other mature technologies, is adapting. Most companies adopted it years earlier to solve the problems of the day: frontend development, service integration, data aggregation, and the general difficulty of getting a large organization’s systems to behave as if they belong to the same company.

But we think the sequencing matters. Are agents causing companies to adopt GraphQL? There’s some early signal that they are. But a more immediately interesting question is whether companies that already adopted GraphQL are better prepared to put agents into production. The answer is an unequivocal “yes.” There is another interesting signal in the Gartner report. GraphQL is in the trough, but Gartner forecasts that it will reach the Plateau of Productivity in less than two years.  That’s sooner than MCP, gRPC, and AI Agent Communication Protocols. In our read, that tells us something about maturity. GraphQL is no longer new enough to receive credit for its potential. It has to earn credit for being useful. That is a healthier place for infrastructure technology to be.

It helps that GraphQL is not a speculative protocol waiting for its first serious workload. It is a Linux Foundation-backed open standard that has been used at enterprise scale for years. This matters when you are choosing infrastructure that could outlive several executive teams, architecture strategies, and AI hype cycles. Proprietary protocols can disappear when their owner’s priorities change. Open standards have a chance to compound.

In our view, Gartner’s own description of GraphQL makes this case more plainly. The report describes its capacity to serve as:

“A unified enterprise data model, decoupled from the underlying service implementations. This shared schema fosters a common understanding of business data across teams, streamlines integration efforts, and accelerates the delivery of new features and digital products. As GraphQL adoption grows, it also supports advanced use cases, such as enterprisewide orchestration and AI integration, further amplifying its business value.”

You could remove “AI integration” from that paragraph and it would still describe why many organizations adopted GraphQL in the first place. Put it back in, though, and the connection becomes pretty obvious. Agents need to find data, understand how it relates, retrieve what they are allowed to retrieve, and take actions across systems. A governed graph does not solve the entire agent problem—nothing does—but it gives agents a coherent surface over systems that were not designed with agents in mind.

American Airlines is a useful example because its story does not begin with an LLM, but it ends with one.

Its core system of record is SABRE, which dates to the 1960s. Years before every software roadmap acquired an “agentic” section, the company built a federated graph spanning customer, loyalty, reservations, and check-in experiences across web, mobile, and kiosks. When its CEO later asked the organization to put AI agents into production on a 90-day delivery cycle, the company did not also have to invent a context layer from scratch. It had already done the foundational architecture work.

As Senior Principal Architect Pragadeesh Prakasam recently explained at the 2026 AI Agent Conference, the team placed Apollo’s MCP Server on top of the graph it already operated. Persisted queries became the agents’ tool surface. Existing field-level security scopes applied to agent interactions. Authentication, governance, and observability were not exciting new items on an AI infrastructure backlog; they were capabilities the company already had.

“We could just focus on the experience,” Prakasam said. “Not on rebuilding the plumbing.”

This is the part we think gets lost when people compare adoption curves. GraphQL did not need to arrive wearing an AI costume to be useful for AI. American Airlines built a graph to solve one generation of software problems and discovered that the same investment helped with the next one. Booking.com, Indeed, and Yahoo! have followed a similar pattern: build a mature, governed graph, then give agents access to that foundation.

So yes, Gartner is right that GraphQL has not spread through agent use cases with the speed or visibility of MCP. But that is a claim about adoption speed, not about value. GraphQL can still be valuable infrastructure for agents even if agents are not yet driving much new adoption of it. In practice, some of the companies best positioned to ship agents today are the ones that built the graph first. We do not think that is a coincidence.

The report’s treatment of AI gateways makes the connection even more interesting. Gartner defines an AI gateway as:

“A tool that acts as an intermediary between applications and various artificial intelligence services or models. Its purpose is to simplify and manage connectivity between AI applications, agents, LLMs and enterprise applications by providing a central point to enable security, governance and observability of AI workloads.”

Most AI gateways today focus on traffic management: model routing, rate limits, token controls, and defenses against attacks such as prompt injection. We at Apollo believe that all of that is necessary. It is also insufficient.

A gateway can control where a request goes without understanding what the underlying data means. It can know that an agent is allowed to call an API without knowing whether the agent should see a particular customer field returned by that API. Without a semantic model underneath it, an AI gateway risks becoming a very sophisticated traffic cop. That’s useful, but lacking the semantics to answer many of the authorization and governance questions that make managing enterprise agents difficult.

Our bet is that the category will move toward combining both layers: gateway controls for AI traffic and a governed model of enterprise data and capabilities. Agents need routing and rate limits, but they also need context. They need to know what systems contain, how concepts relate, what actions are available, and what a particular user or agent is authorized to see.

In our view, Apollo GraphOS can play that role when it is implemented as a context layer for agents. It provides a centralized way to control, observe, and govern what agents do across tools and APIs, using the same federated graph that companies such as American Airlines, Indeed, and Yahoo! already operate in production. The field-level access controls, authentication, and governance are not decorations added after the agent demo gets executive attention. They are part of the graph. The ceiling is much higher with these capabilities in hand.

MCP and GraphQL solve different and complementary problems, and American Airlines’ architecture is interesting precisely because it uses both. The hard part of enterprise agents is providing the model useful context while preserving the security, governance, and observability the organization already requires. Companies with a mature graph have a head start because they have already spent years doing that work.

Call it the trough if you want. We call it a head start.

If you are sorting through what GraphQL, MCP, AI gateways, and the growing pile of agent protocols mean for your architecture, Apollo is offering a complimentary copy of the full 2026 Gartner Hype Cycle for APIs research. If you want to talk through how GraphQL fits into your API strategy, get in touch.

fullText:
James Cameron’s high-octane film sequel is a blueprint for modern action space slashers

Don’t get Pushing Buttons delivered to your inbox? 
It is difficult to believe that James Cameron’s Aliens was released into cinemas 40 years ago. The seminal space shooter took the original Alien – a tense slasher film with a tiny cast and one monster – and transformed it into an intergalactic war movie crammed with wry one-liners, massive guns and an actual boss battle finale. As a 14-year-old, I stood in line at the Tatton Gatley cinema, unsure if I’d be allowed in – I came out three hours later a changed person, my head filled with esoteric military slang and a deep fear of beeping motion detectors. For days afterwards, I slept with my duvet covering my mouth so that no facehuggers could get me. (I was a highly impressionable teenager.)

It’s little wonder that the film has had such a profound effect on video game design. Take the colonial marines, for example. Although the concept of the space soldier had been around in sci-fi novels since the 1930s, most notably in the works of EE “Doc” Smith and Robert Heinlein (the Starship Troopers), Hicks, Hudson, Vasquez and co, were the perfect 80s rendition, combining the witty banter of contemporary buddy cop flicks with awesome weaponry and hi-tech gadgets. Their influence is easy to spot in Doom, where the nameless marine fights ceaseless waves of hellish monsters using a mix of futuristic rifles and good old shotguns. It’s there too in the Halo series, the Spartan soldiers sporting the same armour and mega weapons, cruising about in very similar highly militarised starships and fighting recognisable hive-mind space beasts. Gears of War, Killzone and Marathon all borrow from the same set of costumes and deadly accessories.

Also important to future game designers was the way in which James Cameron opened up the world of Alien after Ridley Scott’s original locked-room mystery of a movie. He beefed up the Weyland-Yutani Corporation, giving us the stencil for dozens of evil video game mega corps; he brought in an array of weapons from handguns to M41A pulse rifles and the M56 smart guns, introducing the idea of a scaled armoury to discover and master; and he employed a structure based around the repeated rhythm of tense exploration followed by explosive encounters that countless games would follow.

It’s weird, then, how difficult it has proven to directly translate the movie into games. While the original Alien spawned a cult 8bit translation and the brilliant Alien: Isolation, Cameron’s sequel is best known for the disastrously bugged Aliens: Colonial Marines, which led to a lawsuit for deceptive marketing. Elsewhere, third-person co-op blaster Aliens: Fireteam Elite drew mixed reviews but has at least birthed a forthcoming sequel, and the 2D Metroid-style game Aliens: Infestation has plenty of fans. My favourite, though, was one of the two official tie-ins from 1986. Aliens: the Computer Game from Electric Dreams Software was a thrilling proto-FPS, allowing you to control several of the movie’s characters as they stalked through an atmosphere processing plant getting attacked by xenomorphs and facehuggers. I’m not sure it’s ever been bettered.

Watching the movie again this week, it’s impossible not to notice all the little scenic and narrative touches that have since shaped how sci-fi action games function. Even the sentry gun, which was cut from the cinematic release and only turned up in the special edition home release, has become a staple special weapon, present in everything from Call of Duty to Helldivers. I wonder how many of today’s game creators were also stood in cinema lines in the summer of 1986, too young to be there, not quite ready to have their minds blown for ever?

Those of us with an interest in the fibre arts are always delighted to see them crop up in other media. Here, embroidered character art helps Scarlet Deer Inn to stand out in a crowded market. Once players are in, they’ll find the charming medieval village has some horrific secrets. Players guide mother-of-two Elise through danger-filled caverns on a quest to find her children and prevent them from meeting a gruesome end, a goal that gained additional meaning when the husband-and-wife developers had a baby of their own. Armed only with a torch, you must keep it lit or likely repeatedly succumb to the darkness. Jordan Erica Webber

Available on: PC

 Estimated playtime: four hours

In what is likely to become a familiar problem for the games industry, Rockstar’s Grand Theft Auto VI marketing schedule is being infiltrated by AI-generated trailers purporting to show scenes from the forthcoming game. Examples include a surfing video and a woman enjoying champagne on a yacht. As Eurogamer points out, the videos are filling a vacuum left by Rockstar’s somewhat stingy approach to releasing in-game footage. The company does not seem to be impressed.

Rather embarrassingly for console manufacturers seeking to go digital only, network outages are back. On Friday, PlayStation Network went down for several hours, leaving players with no access to their games. And on Monday, it was the turn of Xbox, a major outage making it impossible to sign in to user accounts, launch games or download content. While the PlayStation situation has now been resolved, the Xbox network was still having issues at time of press. All hail our disc-less future!

When Valve announced its new Steam Machine PC, fans were intrigued by a custom front plate the company had attached to the machine, which appeared to be an e-ink screen displaying performance data from inside the computer, such as memory and CPU performance. Now, Valve has released all the files and details for what it calls The Inkterface, so owners can build one – and gaming site Aftermath has done just that. Very nerdy, but very cool.

And if you enjoyed reminiscing about Aliens, you might want to check out forthcoming book Aliens: The Video Games by Mike Diver, a complete history of adaptations, including lots of developer interviews.

Silent Hill Townfall: the series is coming to Scotland, but what fresh horrors will it bring?

Glitched into empty space: why video games are obsessed with the Backrooms

Haex – a wilder, weirder open-world adventure

‘An anthem for the co-dependent’: Bad Magpie’s corvid carnage with a side of existential angst

There Are No Ghosts at the Grand – stripping back the physical and metaphorical layers of a haunted hotel

The best gaming chairs in the UK for comfort, support and serious play in 2026 – tested

The Mermaid Mask – the funniest underwater murder mystery you can play | ★★★★☆

This week’s question is from Ben via email:

“I want to learn more about the history of video games and I wondered if there are any canonical lists of the best titles – perhaps a gaming equivalent of the BFI’s 250 Greatest Films of All Time or the American Film Institute’s 100 Years 100 Movies?”

Many publications that write about video games have their own top 100 list, although these tends to be compiled by their own critics or readers rather than a broader spread of experts. GQ, GameRant and Rolling Stone all have versions, while IGN has a “mathematically derived” list of the top 500, and we’ve done the best games of the 21st century (so far). For more formal attempts at developing a canon, the Strong Museum has a World Video Game Hall of Fame, MoMA has a games collection (but for some reason its website does NOT want you to find a definitive list!), and for its Art of Games exhibition in 2012, the Smithsonian compiled a list of 80 important titles with the help of gamers and game makers. There have also been a few books on the subject: try Penguin’s 1001 Video Games You Must Play Before You Die (full disclosure: I wrote some of this book), BFI’s 100 Video Games, or Game On!: From Pong to Oblivion – The Greatest Video Games of All Time, compiled by ex-Edge magazine writers.

If you have a question for Question Block – or anything else to say about the newsletter – email us at pushingbuttons@theguardian.com.

title: Can’t hear what’s playing on TV? It’s not your ears, it’s the flat screen. These affordable soundbars can help
description: Get rid of subtitles to hear what movies and TV shows are supposed to sound like – for as little as...
fullText:
Get rid of subtitles to hear what movies and TV shows are supposed to sound like – for as little as $130

I tested 42 pairs of wireless earbuds to find the best in the US, and I never want to listen to Fast Car again

Your TV sounds awful. That’s not an indictment of your shopping skills, your budget or even the TV’s manufacturer. It’s just basic physics.

The tiny speakers crammed in modern flat-screen TVs simply can’t reproduce the physical sound waves as well as the larger speakers in older TVs. And you don’t need to crave window-rattling action sequences to notice the problem. It also shows up in television shows, making dialog difficult to hear.

You don’t need captions; you need better speakers. And for most people, the easiest, fastest, most affordable option is a simple soundbar.

While every other TV feature has gotten better over the last two decades, from streaming apps to wildly improved picture quality, sound quality has regressed. As a pro who has reviewed dozens of TVs and speakers over the past decade, it’s impossible to miss. Frustratingly, the svelter and more premium your TV, the worse it likely sounds. That’s because those razor-thin TVs contain speakers barely bigger than what you’d find in singing greeting cards.

Luckily, you don’t have to spend three grand on a sprawling eight-channel home theater to vastly improve your TV sound. Setting aside just over $100 for a standalone soundbar can get you there.

Not just any soundbar. After over a decade reviewing them, I’m the first to admit there are plenty of duds that create more problems than they solve. But if you know where to look, you can get a lot for your money, leading to more immersive viewing, deeper engagement and much clearer dialogue, so you can drop those pesky subtitles.

These are my favorite soundbars at multiple price points to help you turn your TV’s sound from a problem to a pleasure.

Vizio soundbars have a reputation for outperforming their modest price points, and the Vizio AIO is the latest embodiment. It captures the company’s typical sound-first design in a stylish minimalist package. At just 34in across and under 3in high, the AIO fits well even in small living rooms and bedrooms. Its fabric-wrapped tubular frame virtually disappears on your console.

You won’t get many extras here, not even a dedicated remote, but you shouldn’t need one: modern TVs let you control volume and power through the TV remote, as long as you connect it through an HDMI ARC or eARC port. Vizio’s app unlocks the rest, including settings such as EQ, sound modes and basic playback control. There’s no wifi, but Bluetooth lets you stream music from your phone or other devices.

It’s the performance that really sets this bar apart, offering surprisingly bombastic bass for its size, full-bodied higher frequencies for instruments such as strings and horns, and clear dialogue. While it’s not the most dynamic bar for music, you’ll enjoy solid detail and balance across registers. At this price, it’s hard to do better for a plug-and-play model.

Another system that puts performance above extras, Sony’s Theater Bar 5 is a ringer for its size. Its simple bar-and-subwoofer setup makes it great for small to moderate-sized rooms. Sony stripped out features such as wifi, an equalizer, or even much of a visual display to focus on sound quality. It pays off, providing a pleasing mix of musicality and power for your money. There’s even a dedicated center speaker to keep dialogue out front, something many soundbars at this price lack.

If you’re tight on space, you may initially balk at the subwoofer, which takes up a few feet of floor space. But subwoofers aren’t just for explosions or kick drums. They’re key to truly impactful performance for everything from action films to dramas and music. Most importantly, the Bar 5 does a great job blending its low-end punch with its crisp sound above for a seamlessly smooth delivery.

You’ll also get Bluetooth streaming and some virtual surround sound tricks, including support for 3D audio formats such as Dolby Atmos and DTS:X. The effect is limited without dedicated surround or up-firing speakers to provide the spherical immersion for which these formats strive, but Sony’s acoustic wizardry expands the soundstage beyond the bar’s physical footprint.

For a smaller system loaded with features, Bose’s taut Smart Soundbar is the best mini-bar I’ve tested. At just 27in across and 2.2in tall, the Smart Soundbar feels more like a Bluetooth speaker than a capable audio system, but its looks are deceiving. Five integrated speakers combine for clean, tactful and surprisingly musical performance, shining through in everything you play.

Unlike Sonos’ rival Beam, the Smart Soundbar even includes up-firing drivers for immersive sound that draws you in, especially with Dolby Atmos video. Like the other bars on our list, Bose’s system connects over HDMI ARC/eARC for simplified control with your TV remote, but you’ll also get a dedicated remote and a great app for multiple ways to play.

That’s just the tip of the bar’s perks, which includes wifi connectivity for high-quality streaming from apps such as Spotify and Apple Music, an equalizer, sound modes, and the ability to connect with other Bose speakers. You can even connect Bose’s fancy Ultra Open earbuds as wearable surround sound speakers. The bar’s biggest drawback is its limited bass response. You can add a Bose subwoofer later (albeit at a high cost), but even without it, the Smart Soundbar serves up best-in-class performance.

Here are a few of my other favorites in other styles and price points.

This powerful standalone soundbar can be expanded with additional components as your needs change, but skips features such as wifi to keep the price low.

The ultimate one-piece soundbar can also be expanded with other Sonos gear for a multi-room sound or surround sound, offering the best of all worlds.

You’ll need to make room for its wireless subwoofer and surround speakers, but this older iteration of Samsung’s multi-piece soundbar system offers incredibly thrilling surround sound from a single box at half the price of the current model.
